premises.text: Conventional e-commerce search assumes buyers know what they want and makes shopping solitary, while friends actually drive product discovery
premises.evidence_span: commerce has really focused on our needs. The ever-present search metaphor presumes that we only want what we know

premises.text: Aspirational brands are curated into a daily personalized store based on what you and friends like, showing who peeked at each product
premises.evidence_span: We use what you and your friends like on Sneak Peek to create a store every single day just for you

premises.text: Limited daily peeks intelligently drop price for everyone peeking until someone buys, creating urgency and competition
premises.evidence_span: every peek drops the price for everyone peeking

premises.text: The experience runs on the web, inside Facebook, and on tablets
premises.evidence_span: Sneak Peek works on sneakpeek.com. It works inside the comforts of Facebook

premises.text: Long-term brand partnerships deliver impulse sales and social-channel engagement for brands
premises.evidence_span: we form long-term partnerships, and we help them deliver meaningful sales

value.text: Social proof and serendipity move shoppers from discovery to purchase
value.evidence_span: This adds the social proof we all need to move us from discovery to purchase

causal_links.evidence_span: friends do help friends discover products
having social or friends data in it really helps people move from discovery to the purchase phase
game mechanics, such as competition and urgency, really drive sales
help them deliver meaningful sales, which are mostly impulse

notes: Three learnings (serendipity, social data, game mechanics) map to separately asserted mechanisms; peek pricing kept as its own domain. Pilot peek counts and $10 credit excluded as traction/promo. Surfaces (web/FB/tablet) folded into social shopping delivery rather than three premises.
